add.issue.name: State worktree honours attributes a writer committed

edit.description.md:
The host checks out the board's state branch as a real worktree (`worktreeAdd`, `rebaseOnto` in `source/git/git-commands.ts`), without the guards linked-repo clones get (`cloneGitConfig` in `source/git/git-utils.ts`: `attr.tree`, hooks off, and so on).

Anyone who can push to the board repo, such as a sandboxed agent, can commit a `.gitattributes` there. On checkout or rebase it triggers filters the user configured globally, git-lfs being the usual one, and a committed `.lfsconfig` can point git-lfs at another server. Hooks and config never travel over git, so this is not arbitrary code, but it is the host acting on files the sandbox wrote.

Not reproduced yet; reasoned from the code and from git's semantics.

Options:
- Apply the attribute guard (`attr.tree=refs/epiq/no-attributes`) to every git call in the state worktree.
- Read and write the log without a checkout (plumbing only).
- Document the server-side fix only: branch protection, plus a push rule that allows nothing but log files.

Parked: jola wants to understand it before deciding.
